authors: Soham Mallick; Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen; Edgar Dobriban; Yonghoon Lee
title: Generalized Hierarchical Conformal Prediction (GHCP)
what_it_holds: Read the arXiv HTML via a fetch tool that returns summaries, not the full text. The paper says HCP cannot use a few observations already collected from the test group, and GHCP does by giving the test group a randomly donated reference-group size and calibrating on retained reference groups plus the observed test-group scores. It claims finite-sample coverage of at least 1-alpha under group exchangeability, group-size ignorability and within-group i.i.d. sampling. Simulations use K=20 reference groups; a secondary review blurb says mean width falls about 60% from o=0 to o=20. I did not see numbers for K=10 or any comparison with a test-group-only conformal set; the intro only says own-group split conformal with few points may be uninformative. Section titles mention width improvements over HCP and 'benefit of within-group training'. The text names HCP as Lee et al. (2026), not Dunn et al.

authors: Robin Dunn; Larry Wasserman; Aaditya Ramdas
title: Distribution-Free Prediction Sets for Two-Layer Hierarchical Models
what_it_holds: From the arXiv and JASA listing abstracts only. Proposes CDF pooling, single subsampling and repeated subsampling for unsupervised and supervised settings, compared on coverage and average set size. Recommends repeated subsampling when a coverage guarantee is wanted and CDF pooling when asymptotic coverage is enough. The abstract says nothing on using labelled units of the new group. [from abstract only]. Note that the GHCP paper calls its HCP baseline the Lee et al. method, so check which paper the claim means by HCP.

authors: Yonghoon Lee; Rina Foygel Barber; Rebecca Willett
title: Distribution-free inference with hierarchical data (HCP, HCP^2)
what_it_holds: Read the HTML via a summarising fetch. Splits groups into K0 groups to train the score and K1 groups to calibrate, weighting each observation by 1/((K1+1)N_k). Marginal coverage at least 1-alpha under hierarchical exchangeability, and at most 1-alpha+2/(K1+1) when scores are distinct. Only the first test-group point is the test point and the remaining test points are ignored, so no labelled target units are used. This is the HCP of the GHCP paper's baseline.

authors: Soham Mallick et al. (repository soham-penn)
title: hierarchical_CP code for GHCP (HCP++ and HCP.sample)
what_it_holds: README read via summarising fetch. Simulations vary the number of observed test points o in {1,15,20,50}, with 20 calibration groups, alpha=0.1, 100 test groups. Real data: ACS income (25 train, 24 test states, 90%) and blood pressure (17 train, 15 test clinics, 80%). Reported at 90% on ACS: HCP.sample width about 1.91 at 90% coverage, HCP about 2.25 at 92%, Pooling about 1.99 at 91%, HCP++ about 2.52 at 99% with 5.2% infinite sets. No own-group-only baseline and no K=10 setting appear in the README. Names here may differ from the paper's names for the methods.

authors: John C. Duchi; Suyash Gupta; Kuanhao Jiang; Pragya Sur
title: Predictive Inference in Multi-environment Scenarios
what_it_holds: Read via summarising fetch. Multi-environment jackknife-minmax and split conformal give (alpha,delta) coverage for a new environment: with probability 1-delta, at least 1-alpha of its examples are covered. With few training environments jackknife-minmax gives smaller sets than split conformal, and with many split conformal does better. A resizing method uses 'limited information from the test environment' to shrink sets, with notable reductions for hierarchical conformal prediction; the summary did not say whether those test points are labelled. The paper is cited by GHCP as the most relevant few-shot work.

authors: Edgar Dobriban; Mengxin Yu
title: SymmPI: Predictive Inference for Data with Group Symmetries
what_it_holds: Read via summarising fetch. General group-symmetry framework with coverage at least nominal and not much above, via number of group orbits. Includes a two-layer hierarchical model with K sub-populations, where the method adaptively centres observations at the sub-population mean or the grand mean depending on heterogeneity. That is close to centring on the target mean for C10. Observed-test-group units enter through an observation function. I did not see widths versus HCP or a K=10 study.

authors: Adam Fisch; Tal Schuster; Tommi Jaakkola; Regina Barzilay
title: Few-shot Conformal Prediction with Auxiliary Tasks
what_it_holds: Read via summarising fetch. Meta-learning view: exchangeable auxiliary tasks tighten sets for a target task with few examples, with marginal coverage over tasks and a (delta, epsilon) sample-conditional variant. Target-task labels are k in-task examples (k=16 per task for chemistry, 160 for image classification). Task-conditional coverage only asymptotic in k. Closest older few-shot analogue to using labelled target-group points plus other groups.

authors: Yichen Shen; Mengxin Yu
title: Conditional Predictive Inference for General Structured Data with Group Symmetries (C-SymmPI)
what_it_holds: Read via summarising fetch. Extends SymmPI to near-conditional coverage over a function class. Covers two-layer hierarchical models and cluster randomized trials, where other individuals' outcomes in the target cluster are observed and only the target outcome is hidden. Near-conditional, not exact, guarantee. No width comparison with HCP seen.

authors: Meshi Bashari; Roy Maor Lotan; Yonghoon Lee; Edgar Dobriban; Yaniv Romano
title: Synthetic-Powered Predictive Inference
what_it_holds: Read via summarising fetch. A small set of m real exchangeable calibration points plus N synthetic points from another distribution, linked by a score transporter. Finite-sample coverage between 1-alpha-beta-epsilon and 1-alpha+beta+epsilon+1/(N+1), with worst-case bounds from m, N, alpha, beta alone. Tighter than split conformal when the two distributions align. Analogous to borrowing from other donors with few target labels, but not a cluster setting.

authors: Yi Liu; Alexander W. Levis; Sharon-Lise Normand; Larry Han
title: Multi-Source Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
what_it_holds: Read via summarising fetch. K sites with one target; uses observed target-site outcomes and, under common conditional outcome distribution, source outcomes, with data-adaptive up-weighting of informative sources. Coverage is nominal plus O_P(n^-1/2 + nuisance-error product), not exact finite-sample. Marginal guarantee. Relevant to combining other-site data with target labels.

authors: Yonghoon Lee; Zhimei Ren
title: Selection from Hierarchical Data with Conformal e-values
what_it_holds: Read via summarising fetch. Conformal e-values under hierarchical exchangeability, with e-BH controlling group-size-conditional FDR. Selection, not prediction sets.

authors: David Broska; Michael Howes
title: Cluster-Robust Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Abstract only, read through a third-party listing page. Cluster-Robust PPI++ gives closed-form standard errors under arbitrary within-cluster dependence and handles partially labelled clusters. The authors analyse how the labelling design affects precision and derive a cluster-aware power-tuning rule. Standard PPI++ covered under 60% in a TV news application. Does not mention prediction sets [from abstract only]. Closest item to C11 inference side, and very recent.

authors: Virginia L. Ma; Emmanuel J. Candes
title: Optimized Labeling Resource Allocation for Prediction-Assisted Inference via OPAL
what_it_holds: Read via summarising fetch. Learns a smooth labelling-probability policy as a function of an uncertainty score to minimise estimator variance under an expected-budget constraint, solved as a convex program. Estimands include log odds ratio and influence-function functionals. No prediction sets or clusters.

authors: Andrew Ilyas; Joonhyuk Ko; Jingwu Tang; Steven Wu; Jiahao Zhang
title: Provably Label-Efficient Conformal Prediction
what_it_holds: Poster abstract only. Online stopping rule for how many labels to query for conformal calibration, trading labelling cost against set size, with expected cost matching the best fixed calibration size in hindsight and about 40.6% cost reduction versus common fixed sizes. Prediction-set side of a budget, but no inference or cluster component. [from abstract only]

authors: Daniel Csillag; Pedro Dall'Antonia; Claudio Jose Struchiner; Guilherme Tegoni Goedert
title: Extending Prediction-Powered Inference through Conformal Prediction
what_it_holds: Read via summarising fetch. Imputes through a calibrated conformal set-predictor. Labelled hold-out data serve only the conformal step, and inference uses only unlabelled covariates, with bounds widened by M times the miscoverage rate. Links PPI and conformal but does not split one budget between the two goals.

authors: Charlie Cowen-Breen; Alekh Agarwal; Stephen Bates; William W. Cohen; Jacob Eisenstein; Amir Globerson; Adam Fisch
title: Multiple-Prediction-Powered Inference (MultiPPI)
what_it_holds: Abstract level only. Allocates a budget across expensive measurements and several cheaper proxies for estimation, with minimax and asymptotic-normality claims. Budget allocation for inference only.

authors: Daniela Corbetta; Livio Finos; Ludwig Geistlinger; Davide Risso
title: Conformal inference for cell type annotation with graph-structured constraints (scConform)
what_it_holds: Read via summarising fetch. Conformal sets for cell types respecting ontology structure, on MERFISH spatial transcriptomics (random cell-level splits) and scRNA-seq COVID data with one donor held out (43 donors). Authors attribute remaining overcoverage to systematic patient differences. Closest conformal-in-spatial/single-cell item found; classification and no donor-level calibration.
